claim: The exact etiology of UC remains elusive.
source: The exact etiology of UC remains elusive.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about the unknown causes of UC.

claim: IBDs are caused by dysregulated immune responses against components of the microbiota and intestinal wall in genetically susceptible individuals.
source: Available evidence suggests that IBDs are caused by dysregulated immune responses against components of the microbiota and intestinal wall in genetically susceptible individuals (Xavier and Podolsky, 2007; Chang, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Xavier and Podolsky, 2007 and Chang, 2020.

claim: The innate immunity is equally as important as adaptive immunity in the pathogenesis of IBDs.
source: The adaptive immunity is classically considered to play a major role in the pathogenesis of IBDs; however, accumulating evidence has shown that the innate immunity is equally as important (Geremia et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Geremia et al., 2014.

claim: IBDs may result from impaired functioning of the intestinal innate immune system.
source: IBDs may result from impaired functioning of the intestinal innate immune system, which is comprised of the epithelial barrier and a variety of innate immune cells, including neutrophils, monocytes/macrophages, and dendritic cells (Parikh et al., 2019; Drury et al., 2021; Na et al., 2019; Shale and Ghosh, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Parikh et al., 2019; Drury et al., 2021; Na et al., 2019; Shale and Ghosh, 2009).

claim: GM-CSF and IL-3 are hematopoietic growth factors for the myeloid lineage mainly functioning under inflammatory conditions.
source: Granulocyte–macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) and Interleukin-3 (IL-3) are a group of hematopoietic growth factors for the myeloid lineage mainly functioning under inflammatory conditions (Becher et al., 2016; Dougan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Becher et al., 2016 and Dougan et al., 2019.

claim: GM-CSF and IL-3 regulate various inflammatory responses that promote rapid clearance of pathogens while contributing to the persistence of chronic inflammation.
source: They regulate various inflammatory responses that promote rapid clearance of pathogens while contribute to the persistence of chronic inflammation (Dougan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dougan et al., 2019.

claim: GM-CSF and IL-3 mediate the cross-talk between innate and adaptive immunity.
source: Besides, these cytokines also mediate the cross-talk between innate and adaptive immunity (Dougan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dougan et al., 2019.

claim: The receptors for GM-CSF and IL-3 are both heteromers comprising a ligand-specific α subunit and a shared β common subunit (CD131).
source: The receptors for GM-CSF and IL-3, expressed on various immune cells, are both heteromers comprising a ligand-specific α subunit (CD116 and CD123, respectively) and a shared β common subunit (CD131) (Becher et al., 2016; Dougan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Becher et al., 2016 and Dougan et al., 2019.

claim: The α chains of GM-CSF and IL-3 receptors provide specificity for the cytokines but bind with relatively low affinity.
source: The α chains provide specificity for the cytokines but bind with relatively low affinity, while their association with the β common chain provides high affinity necessary for effective downstream signaling (Broughton et al., 2012; Hansen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Broughton et al., 2012 and Hansen et al., 2008.

claim: The association of α chains with the β common chain provides high affinity necessary for effective downstream signaling.
source: The α chains provide specificity for the cytokines but bind with relatively low affinity, while their association with the β common chain provides high affinity necessary for effective downstream signaling (Broughton et al., 2012; Hansen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Broughton et al., 2012 and Hansen et al., 2008.

claim: GM-CSF delivers pleiotropic effects, either pro- or anti-inflammatory, on intestinal inflammation depending on the cellular and cytokine milieu as well as disease model.
source: For instance, GM-CSF has been shown to deliver pleiotropic effects, either pro- or anti-inflammatory, on the intestinal inflammation depending on the cellular and cytokine milieu as well as disease model (Castro-Dopico et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Castro-Dopico et al., 2020 and Xu et al., 2008.

claim: IBD is characterized by impaired expression and function of CD116 in circulating granulocytes and monocytes.
source: For example, a previous study showed that IBD was characterized by impaired expression and function of CD116 in circulating granulocytes and monocytes, suggesting a defect in innate immunity in response to GM-CSF (Goldstein et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Goldstein et al., 2011.

claim: A frameshift mutation in CSF2RB gene is associated with higher risk for Crohn's disease and reduced monocyte signaling in response to GM-CSF in Ashkenazi Jewish populations.
source: Besides, in a genetic analysis of Ashkenazi Jewish populations that have a high prevalence of Crohn's disease, a frameshift mutation in CSF2RB gene (encoding CD131) was shown associated with higher risk for Crohn's disease and reduced monocyte signaling in response to GM-CSF (Chuang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chuang et al., 2016.

claim: Csf2rb gene expression appears to elevate with time in murine colon tissues in response to DSS administration.
source: The expression of Csf2rb appeared to elevate with time, but only until day 6 a significantly increased Csf2rb expression was demonstrated (Figure 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of gene expression dataset GSE22307 and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Csf2rb mRNA expression is significantly elevated in the distal part of the colon of wt mice following 7 days of 2% DSS administration compared to mice receiving normal drinking water.
source: We then subjected our wt mice to 2% DSS in the drinking water for 7 days to establish murine colitis and found that Csf2rb mRNA expression was significantly elevated in the distal part of the colon comparing to mice receiving normal drinking water (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Csf2rb mRNA could not be effectively detected in the proximal part of the colon.
source: The Csf2rb mRNA could not be effectively detected in the proximal part of the colon and therefore only the distal colon was used for further analyses.
evidence: This is a methodological observation from the experimental data.

claim: No significant change in Csf2rb mRNA expression level was found in blood leukocytes, intra-peritoneal lavage cells, mesenteric lymph nodes, spleen, and thymus following DSS administration.
source: Nevertheless, we could not find any significant change in Csf2rb mRNA expression level in other immune-related tissues, including blood leukocytes, intra-peritoneal lavage cells, mesenteric lymph nodes, spleen, and thymus, following DSS administration (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–e.

claim: Il3ra gene expression shows a significant increase in the colon tissues at day 6 of DSS administration in the gene expression dataset.
source: The gene expression dataset analysis also showed a tendency of increase in Csf2ra (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f) and a significant increase in Il3ra (Figure 1—figure supplement 1g), which encode the α subunit of GM-CSF and IL-3 receptors, respectively, in the colon tissues at day 6 of DSS administration.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression dataset analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1g.

claim: No change in Csf2ra mRNA expression level was found in the colon tissues of wt mice following DSS administration.
source: Whereas, we did not find any change in Csf2ra mRNA expression level in the colon tissues of our mice following DSS administration (Figure 1—figure supplement 1h), while Il3ra mRNA could not be effectively detected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1i).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1h.

claim: Il3ra mRNA could not be effectively detected in murine colon tissues.
source: Whereas, we did not find any change in Csf2ra mRNA expression level in the colon tissues of our mice following DSS administration (Figure 1—figure supplement 1h), while Il3ra mRNA could not be effectively detected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1i).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1i.

claim: Wt mice showed reduced body weight in response to DSS administration compared to CD131-deficient mice.
source: While the wt mice showed reduced body weight, shortened colon length, as well as more tissue destruction seen on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, increased CD11b+Ly6G+ neutrophil infiltration, and Tnf and Il1b mRNA expression in their colon tissues in response to DSS; the CD131-deficient mice were generally protected from the effects of DSS (Figure 1c–g, Figure 1—figure supplement 2a, b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: CD131 contributed to the effects of DSS on inducing murine colitis.
source: These demonstrated that CD131 contributed to the effects of DSS on inducing murine colitis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing wt and CD131-deficient mice.

claim: Homozygous Csf2rb knock-out mice are fatal at an early stage.
source: We could only have heterozygous Csf2rb knock-out mice, while the homozygous ones were fatal at an early stage.
evidence: This is an observation from the breeding of CD131-deficient mice.

source: Nevertheless, the Tnf and Il1b mRNA expression in blood leukocytes, as well as the neutrophils in the blood, were comparable between DSS-treated and control wt mice (Figure 1i, j), indicating a local, but not systemic, inflammation in our model.

claim: Neutrophils in the blood were comparable between DSS-treated and control wt mice.
source: Nevertheless, the Tnf and Il1b mRNA expression in blood leukocytes, as well as the neutrophils in the blood, were comparable between DSS-treated and control wt mice (Figure 1i, j), indicating a local, but not systemic, inflammation in our model.

claim: The DSS-induced murine colitis model represents a local, but not systemic, inflammation.
source: Nevertheless, the Tnf and Il1b mRNA expression in blood leukocytes, as well as the neutrophils in the blood, were comparable between DSS-treated and control wt mice (Figure 1i, j), indicating a local, but not systemic, inflammation in our model.

source: Immune cell infiltration analysis showed that the M1 subtype of macrophages and γδT cells were significantly enriched in the colonic tissues of DSS-treated wt mice, suggesting the association between CD131 and the infiltration of these cell subpopulations (Figure 2a).

evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Several innate and acquired immune-related pathways were enriched in wt mice compared to CD131-deficient mice.
source: Besides, several innate and acquired immune-related pathways, including antigen processing and presentation, FcγR-mediated phagocytosis, FcεRI signaling pathway, Toll-like receptor signaling pathway, natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity, cell adhesion molecules, TNF signaling pathway, bacterial invasion of epithelial cells, T cell receptor signaling pathway, Th1 and Th2 cell differentiation, Th17 cell differentiation, and B cell receptor signaling pathway, were also enriched in wt mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There were 1411 DEGs between control and DSS-treated wt mice.
source: There were 1411 DEGs between control and DSS-treated wt mice, as well as 17,760 non-DEGs between the CD131-deficient mice; the intersection resulted in 573 genes (Figure 2d, Supplementary file 2), comprising 327 up-regulated and 246 down-regulated genes, for further analyses.
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The up-regulated intersected genes were associated with functions of plasma membrane and synapses.
source: The Gene Ontology enrichment analysis showed that the up-regulated genes were associated with functions of plasma membrane and synapses (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a, Supplementary file 3), while the down-regulated genes were associated with cellular and nuclear activities (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by Gene Ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a.

claim: The down-regulated intersected genes were associated with cellular and nuclear activities.
source: The Gene Ontology enrichment analysis showed that the up-regulated genes were associated with functions of plasma membrane and synapses (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a, Supplementary file 3), while the down-regulated genes were associated with cellular and nuclear activities (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by Gene Ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: The up-regulated intersected genes were involved in protein digestion and absorption, cholinergic synapse, and PI3K–Akt signaling pathways.

claim: The down-regulated intersected genes were involved in cell cycle, progesterone-mediated oocyte maturation, Fanconi anemia, and DNA replication pathways.
